samples.summary: Unbounded `while (true)` parent-chain walk in `resolveNestedTableLayout` is newly reachable from the cell-range paint path; a peer-crafted document with duplicate block IDs can make the walk loop forever (tab hang).
samples.evidence: `resolveNestedTableLayout` walks up `layout.blockParentMap` in `while (true) { const parentInfo = layout.blockParentMap.get(topTableId); if (!parentInfo) break; topTableId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }` (table-layout.ts:479-484) with no visited-set and no depth cap. Block IDs are taken verbatim from peer-written CRDT attributes — `id: attrs.id ?? ''` (crdt-tree.ts:233 and :263) — and nothing in the repo validates uniqueness (grep for `duplicate|unique id|dedupe|seenIds` under packages/docs/src finds no ID-uniqueness check). `computeTableLayout` step 7 writes `blockParentMap.set(block.id, { tableBlockId, ... })` for each cell child including nested table blocks (table-layout.ts:423-431), so two nested tables that share IDs with each other's ancestors produce a chain A->B->A; the map is a flat Map keyed by ID, so last-writer-wins collisions are attacker-shapeable. Attack: a malicious collaborator (or a crafted document served to the victim) writes a nested-table structure with colliding block IDs; the victim drag-selects or shift+clicks cells in that table; the new line `resolveNestedTableLayout(crBlockId, layout)?.dataBlock.tableData` at selection.ts:130 runs on every `normalizeRange`, i.e. every render, and spins in the loop with the main thread pinned — an unrecoverable UI hang, no error surfaced. Note the same loop is already reachable from selection.ts:169 and from `buildCellRangeRects`, so this is an added reachability rather than a wholly new vector; I could not construct the exact CRDT tree that yields the cycle from the tests, hence low confidence. Fix is cheap: bound the walk with a visited `Set` (or a depth counter) and return `undefined` on a cycle, as the adjacent per-segment walk at selection.ts:147-157 also lacks.

samples.summary: Enabling read-time merge expansion for nested tables puts `expandCellRangeForMerges`'s quadratic `findMergeTopLeft` scan on the per-render path for peer-controlled table geometry.
samples.evidence: `normalizeRange` runs on every paint while a cell range is selected. Previously the nested-table lookup returned `undefined` and `normalizeCellRange` skipped expansion (selection.ts:112); after this change the fixed-point loop in `expandCellRangeForMerges` (selection.ts:66-91) runs for nested tables too, and for each covered cell (`cell.colSpan === 0`) it calls `findMergeTopLeft`, which scans `rr` from r down to 0 and `cc` from c down to 0 (selection.ts:33-45) — O(rows·cols) per covered cell, O((rows·cols)^2) per pass. Columns are banded (`MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS = 256`, numeric-attrs.ts:95) and spans are banded (`MAX_TABLE_SPAN = 1000`, numeric-attrs.ts:92), but I found no bound on row count from a peer-written CRDT table, so a collaborator supplying a nested table with very many rows of merged cells makes each frame do quadratic work while a cell range is selected — degraded-to-frozen UI rather than a hard hang. Bounded severity because the same expansion already runs for top-level tables; this only widens where it applies.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as written. `resolveNestedTableLayout` contains a literal `while (true)` parent-chain walk with no visited set and no depth cap (table-layout.ts:479-484), and the follow-up path walk at table-layout.ts:505-510 is similarly unbounded. A cycle in `blockParentMap` is constructible from untrusted data: step 7 registers every cell child — nested table blocks included — as `blockParentMap.set(block.id, { tableBlockId, ... })` (table-layout.ts:423-431), and `layoutCellBlocks` merges each nested table's map into the outer flat map (table-layout.ts:146-150), so a nested table B under top-level A that contains any block with id A yields A->B and B->A; a cell block sharing its own table's id yields a self-edge. Block ids come verbatim from peer-written CRDT attributes with an empty-string fallback (`id: attrs.id ?? ''` at crdt-tree.ts:233 and crdt-tree.ts:263), and I found no uniqueness/dedupe validation anywhere under packages/docs/src (grep for seenIds/dedupe/duplicate-id returned only unrelated image and cursor dedupe at export/docx-exporter.ts:84 and view/text-box-editor.ts:643). Reachability holds: selection.ts:130 calls the resolver on the cell-range path and the preceding `layout.blocks.find` (selection.ts:129) only short-circuits for top-level tables, so a nested-table cell range enters the walk on every normalizeRange; further unguarded call sites at selection.ts:169, selection.ts:299, selection.ts:590, editor.ts:2256, text-editor.ts:4316 and text-editor.ts:4912. Impact is a main-thread infinite loop (unrecoverable tab hang) driven by a malicious collaborator's document — untrusted-input handling / availability, a hazard this codebase explicitly treats as in scope (crdt-tree.ts:223-226 clamps row heights precisely because "an Infinity height never terminates"). No guard renders it unreachable, so there is no ground to refute on.
